# 2 Baruch Chapter 56 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Syriac MS (Codex Ambrosianus 7a1) | **Section:** The Cloud and Waters Vision

---

**1** "The first black waters you saw coming down from the great sea to the earth —"

**2** "— those are the transgressions of Adam, in which Eve his wife was also complicit."

**3** "When he transgressed, untimely death entered, mourning was introduced, affliction was prepared, sickness was created, toil was established, and pride began."

**4** "The realm of the dead began demanding blood for renewal; childbearing came into existence; the suffering of parents began; humanity's greatness was diminished; and goodness faded."

**5** "What could be darker or weightier than all of this? For when Adam sinned and death was decreed on all who would be born, the vast multitude of those who would perish was counted along with it."

**6** "Think for yourself about what Adam did to those of us who came after him — we have all suffered because of him."

**7** "But in this respect Adam is not the cause of anything except his own soul — for each of us has been his own Adam."

**8** "But you might ask: 'What good is it to face judgment after death, when we have sinned against the very Judge?'"

**9** "Now hear the rest of what the first black waters mean: after Adam sinned, a time of grief followed."

**10** "The heavens trembled, and the earth shook from its foundations."

**11** "The creatures of the garden of Eden fled away, and the wild animals took to the forests."

**12** "The angels of the Lord and the heavenly powers pulled back from the glory of the Lord."

**13** "The stars shook at their posts, and the foundations of the earth trembled."

**14** "The angels and the powers of light withdrew from their stations, and the glory of the Lord ascended."

**15** "Darkness moved in and settled, and the voices of the holy ones fell silent."

**16** "All of this happened because of Adam's transgression, and the earth was cast into darkness."

---

*PNEUMA notes: Dynamic equivalence rendering. Prioritizes clarity and natural English flow while preserving the theological and narrative content of the Syriac source.*
